items.stem: What is a realistic expectation for AI in project delivery?

options.text: It can assist with drafting and summarising, with human review and accountability
options.rationale: Correct: AI assists; the PM stays accountable and reviews output.

options.text: It can run the project without human oversight
options.rationale: AI does not replace project leadership or accountability.

options.text: It guarantees schedules will be accurate
It removes the need for stakeholder management

items.explanation: Correct: AI assists with drafting and summarising, under human review and accountability.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when using AI on project documents? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Grounding summaries in real project artifacts
Reviewing AI drafts before they are shared
options.rationale: Correct: human review catches errors and tone issues.

options.text: Entering client-confidential data into a public tool
Sharing an AI-drafted plan with no validation
options.rationale: Unvalidated plans are a delivery risk.

items.explanation: Correct: ground outputs in real artifacts and review drafts before sharing.

items.stem: Who is accountable for an AI-assisted status report sent to a client?

options.text: The project manager, who remains accountable for the output
options.rationale: Correct: accountability stays with the human, not the tool.
The vendor is not accountable for your report.

options.text: No one, because AI produced it
options.rationale: AI involvement does not remove accountability.
The recipient is not accountable for its accuracy.

items.explanation: Correct: the project manager remains accountable for AI-assisted outputs.
